Our team comprises multidisciplinary professionals with strong functional experience in financial applications and robust IT technical backgrounds.

The Digital Finance Transformation Division (DFTD) provides program management services for the design, development, testing, and rollout of group finance solutions.

• Provide expertise and support for the design and implementation of performance reporting and financial analytics, specifically, to drive Actual/Plan/Forecast alignment.
• Analyze and resolve complex system issues, collaborating with the IT team for technical escalation when needed.
• Communicate concepts, artifacts, and findings effectively to technical and business audience.

• Participate in system upgrades, providing expertise and ensuring smooth transitions.

• Obtain necessary technology certifications to stay current with industry trends and best practices.

About Lucidya

Lucidya is an AI-native Customer Experience Intelligence platform that helps organizations understand customer conversations, uncover actionable insights, and improve customer experiences through advanced AI capabilities.

As the platform continues to grow, maintaining reliable, secure, and high-performing data infrastructure is critical to supporting our customers and enabling continuous product innovation.

Our database environment spans multiple cloud platforms and hosting environments, supporting business-critical workloads, high-volume data ingestion, and multi-tenant applications. We are looking for a Database Administrator who can help strengthen our database operations, improve resilience, and ensure our data infrastructure remains reliable as we scale.

Why this role matters

Our database infrastructure is growing in both scale and complexity. With production PostgreSQL and MySQL environments running across AWS, Google Cloud Platform (GCP), and our in-Kingdom hosting environment, maintaining database availability, performance, and recoverability is essential to the reliability of our platform.

As a Database Administrator, you’ll take ownership of the health and operational reliability of our production databases. You’ll work on challenges that go beyond routine administration, including multi-terabyte database environments, high-availability architecture, disaster recovery, major-version upgrades, and safe database migrations.

You’ll also work closely with engineering, cloud, and reliability teams to help developers make better database decisions, prevent production incidents, and improve the way database changes are designed and delivered.

If you enjoy solving complex database performance challenges, building resilient data infrastructure, and taking ownership of critical production systems, this role offers the opportunity to make a meaningful impact.

What You’ll Do
• Manage and maintain PostgreSQL and MySQL databases across AWS, GCP, and self-managed environments.
• Monitor database performance, availability, and capacity.
• Optimize queries, indexing, and database resource utilization.
• Manage backups, point-in-time recovery, and disaster recovery.
• Implement database replication, high availability, and failover strategies.
• Plan database upgrades, migrations, and safe schema changes.
• Maintain database security, access controls, and auditing.
• Automate database operations using Bash, Python, or similar tools.
• Troubleshoot database incidents and perform root-cause analysis.
• Collaborate with engineering, DevOps, SRE, and Cloud teams to improve database reliability and scalability.

What success looks like (First 90–120 Days)

First 30 days:
• You’ve developed a clear understanding of the production database estate across AWS, GCP, and SITE.
• You understand the existing database architecture, operational workflows, monitoring, and recovery procedures.
• You’ve built strong working relationships with the database team, Cloud Engineering, SRE, and development teams.
• You’ve identified the most significant risks and improvement opportunities across availability, performance, backup, and recovery.

By day 60:
• You’re independently handling assigned database administration and troubleshooting activities.
• You’ve reviewed backup configurations and started validating recovery procedures for critical databases.
• You’ve identified gaps in database monitoring and alerting, including replication lag, WAL contention, autovacuum, and table bloat.
• You’re contributing to database performance improvements and operational documentation.

By day 90:
• Critical database restore tests have been completed or are progressing against an agreed recovery-testing plan, with gaps documented and corrective actions defined.
• Key database failure scenarios are documented through practical runbooks.
• Database monitoring and alerting improvements have been implemented for prioritized operational risks.
• You’re actively contributing to database reliability, performance, and incident-prevention initiatives.

By day 120:
• A safer database change-management process is in place, including appropriate reviews, DDL auditing, and rollback planning.
• A practical PostgreSQL major-upgrade roadmap has been developed, with compatibility and migration risks assessed.
• The high-availability approach for the SITE database environment has been evaluated and documented.
• Database size and activity metrics are available to support the per-customer cost-allocation initiative.

You’re comfortable working with large, business-critical databases and can balance operational stability with the need to improve architecture, automation, and scalability.

job_description:
Network Engineer - AI Infrastructure, RDMA & Storage

Description
VAST Data is the data platform company for the AI era. We build enterprise software infrastructure to capture, catalog, refine, enrich, and protect massive datasets, and make them available for real-time data analysis and AI training and inference. Designed from the ground up to make AI simple to deploy and manage, VAST takes the cost and complexity out of deploying enterprise and AI infrastructure across data center, edge, and cloud.

About the Role :

The fastest system in the world is only as fast as the network under it. As a Network Engineer in VAST's Field Engineering organization, you define how VAST connects to the world: the reference architectures, validated switch configurations, and RDMA fabric designs every customer deployment is built on.

This is a design and research role, not a support queue. You will build and run the lab where new switches, NICs, and network operating systems are qualified before they ever reach a customer. You will investigate why a fabric behaves differently at 800G than it did at 100G, and turn the answer into a standard the whole field organization uses. When a strategic customer hits something nobody has seen before, you reproduce it, explain it, and make sure it never happens to the next customer.

You will work across R&D, QA, Support, Product, and customer engineering teams, and directly with networking vendors including NVIDIA, Arista, Cisco, and Juniper. The work sits where AI infrastructure is hardest: GPU fabrics, lossless Ethernet, and storage protocols moving at line rate.

Requirements
What a Day in the Life Looks Like :

Design the Architecture: Define reference network architectures for VAST deployments: L2 and L3 fabrics, BGP and EVPN/VXLAN designs, RoCEv2 and QoS policy. Decide what \"good\" looks like, then write it down so the field can execute it consistently.

Own the Lab: Build and run validation environments for switch qualification, interoperability testing, performance characterization, and reproduction of customer issues. Your lab is where we find problems before customers do.

Qualify the Ecosystem: Evaluate new switches, network operating systems, and NICs from NVIDIA, Arista, Cisco, Juniper, and others. Work directly with vendor engineering teams to close gaps and certify what works.

Solve What Nobody Else Can: Chase complex problems across the full path between GPUs, fabric, and storage. Congestion, packet loss, MTU, latency, PFC and ECN behavior under real load. Root cause it, then fix it at the source.

Turn Findings into Product: Feed what you learn back into VAST, as documented best practice, as automation, and as direct input to R&D on what the platform should do differently.

Professional Experience & Skills

• Strong data center networking fundamentals - CCNP level or equivalent hands-on experience

• Solid command of BGP and L3 routing: eBGP/iBGP, ECMP, route policy, multipath, BGP-based fabrics

• Hands-on experience designing and troubleshooting both L2 and L3 data center networks

• Real troubleshooting ability across layers - routing, ARP/ND, MTU, congestion, packet loss, latency

• Working knowledge of Linux networking: interfaces, VLANs, routing tables, namespaces, MTU

• Comfort with tcpdump, Wireshark, iperf, and the standard diagnostic toolkit

• The instinct to build a lab and reproduce a problem rather than theorize about it

• Clear technical writing - your designs and findings are only useful if others can follow them

Job title: Senior QA Engineer – Manual Testing & Application Monitoring

1. Role Overview

We are seeking an experienced Senior Technical QA Analyst to ensure the functional quality, technical stability and reliability of our digital eCommerce platforms. The role combines hands-on manual testing, API and integration testing, production application monitoring and technical incident investigation.

The candidate will identify functional defects, monitor application errors using Sentry or equivalent observability tools, investigate customer-facing issues and coordinate with internal technology teams and external development vendors. This is not a purely functional manual testing position.

2. Key Responsibilities

A. Functional & Manual Testing
• Develop and execute functional, regression, integration and end-to-end test cases.
• Validate web customer journeys including registration, quotation, checkout, payment and post-purchase transactions.
• Perform browser compatibility, responsive design and mobile web testing.
• Review requirements, UX designs and acceptance criteria for test coverage.
• Document, prioritize and track defects; conduct smoke testing, UAT support and release validation.

B. Application Observability, Monitoring & Production Quality
• Operate application monitoring and observability platforms; investigate production issues across browser, application, API and infrastructure signals.
• Monitor frontend/backend exceptions, failed transactions, API availability, latency, slow page loads, user-impacting errors and performance regressions.
• Correlate stack traces, logs, browser console/network evidence, distributed traces, session replay, release changes and service health to investigate incidents.
• Analyze recurring issues, severity, frequency and customer-journey impact.
• Maintain monitoring dashboards, alerts, thresholds, incident classifications and escalation playbooks; coordinate with IT/vendors on instrumentation gaps.
• Monitor release health and verify resolution of production issues.

C. API & Integration Testing
• Test REST APIs with Postman or equivalent tools, including payloads, authentication and error handling.
• Investigate HTTP errors, timeouts and integration defects.
• Validate integrations among the eCommerce platform, payment gateways, core systems and third-party services.

D. Technical Quality & Incident Management
• Serve as a technical quality contact between business, IT and development vendors.
• Reproduce incidents, provide evidence-backed defect reports and verify fixes.
• Track defect recurrence and release quality; prioritize issues by customer and business impact.

E. Reporting & Continuous Improvement
• Maintain QA execution, defect and application stability reports.
• Track error rates, failed transactions, critical defects, incident recurrence and resolution time.
• Recommend improvements in monitoring coverage, test processes and release quality.

Monitoring & Diagnostic Tool Landscape (examples, not an exhaustive checklist)
• Application error tracking & APM: Sentry, Datadog APM/RUM, New Relic, Dynatrace, Cisco AppDynamics, Elastic Observability, Azure Application Insights, AWS CloudWatch / X-Ray.
• Logs, metrics & infrastructure observability: Grafana, Prometheus, Loki, Elasticsearch / Kibana (ELK), Splunk, OpenSearch, CloudWatch Logs, Azure Monitor.
• Real-user monitoring & session diagnostics: Datadog RUM, New Relic Browser, Dynatrace Digital Experience Monitoring, Sentry Session Replay, LogRocket, FullStory; browser DevTools.
• Synthetic monitoring & availability: Checkly, Pingdom, UptimeRobot, Datadog Synthetic Monitoring, New Relic Synthetics, Grafana Synthetic Monitoring.
• API, network & test diagnostics: Postman, Swagger/OpenAPI, Chrome DevTools, Charles Proxy or Fiddler; Jira/Azure DevOps for incident and defect tracking.
• Candidates need not know every listed product. Require demonstrated depth in at least one observability/APM platform, strong web/API debugging and the ability to learn the organization's chosen stack.

3. Required Qualifications & Experience

Mandatory Requirements
• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, IT or related discipline.
• 4–6+ years in software QA with strong manual web application testing.
• Practical API testing experience using Postman or equivalent.
• Strong knowledge of HTTP, JSON, REST APIs and client-server architecture.
• Proficiency in browser DevTools (Console and Network), JavaScript error investigation and API troubleshooting.
• Experience with Jira, Azure DevOps or equivalent defect/test management tools.
• Experience with complex transactional web applications and engineering/vendor collaboration.

Highly Preferred
• Hands-on production use of at least one application observability/APM platform (e.g., Sentry, Datadog, New Relic, Dynatrace, Elastic Observability, Grafana stack, AppDynamics, Azure Application Insights or AWS CloudWatch).
• Production application support and customer-facing incident investigation.
• Experience interpreting application logs, metrics, traces, exception stack traces, API latency, release health and user-impacting performance signals.
• eCommerce, fintech, banking or insurance platform experience.

• Basic JavaScript or TypeScript; SQL; Playwright, Cypress or Selenium.

Outputs
• Functional, regression and end-to-end test cases and execution reports.

You write production code from your first sprint. You will build the services, APIs, and interfaces that run inside enterprise systems across the UAE and GCC — under the review of architects who read every line, and to engineering standards you will be held to rather than eased into.

• Integrate external APIs and data sources — authentication, pagination, retries, rate limits, and failure handling that does not fall over in production.
• Debug across the stack — reproduce, read logs and traces, isolate the root cause, and fix the cause rather than the symptom.
• Use AI-assisted development environments (Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot) to accelerate delivery — then review, test, and explain what they produced.
• Document what you build — clear READMEs, API contracts, and honest commit and PR descriptions your teammates can work from.
• Participate in design discussions — ask why a design was chosen, propose alternatives, and learn to argue trade-offs rather than preferences.

MUST-HAVE: ENGINEERING FOUNDATION

Programming. Strong Python — clean, readable, tested code; functions and classes, error handling, packages and virtual environments. Equivalent strength in another language plus demonstrable ability to become productive in Python quickly is acceptable.

APIs & Web Services. REST fundamentals and the ability to build an endpoint end to end (FastAPI, Flask, Django, or Node/Express). HTTP semantics, JSON, status codes, and authentication basics.

Front-End. TypeScript/JavaScript and one modern framework — Angular preferred, React acceptable — with solid HTML and CSS. You should be able to put a working interface in front of a service you built.

Databases. SQL that goes beyond SELECT * — joins, aggregation, indexing basics, and sane schema design. PostgreSQL or SQL Server experience preferred.

Version Control & Tooling. Git in daily use (branching, pull requests, resolving merge conflicts), plus fluency in VS Code or Visual Studio and comfort on the command line.

Computer Science Fundamentals. Data structures, algorithmic complexity, object-oriented design, exception handling, and a working understanding of asynchronous execution and concurrency.

Testing. Hands-on with a unit testing framework (pytest, Jest, or equivalent) and able to say what separates a useful test from a decorative one.

AI-Native Development. You already build with AI coding assistants and can explain, line by line, what the tool produced and why it is correct. The AI wrote it is never an explanation for a defect.

GOOD TO HAVE — SIGNALS OF TRAJECTORY
• Docker fundamentals, or a CI/CD pipeline (Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions) you set up yourself rather than inherited.
• Cloud exposure — Azure preferred; AWS or GCP equally welcome as evidence you can operate beyond localhost.
• Calling an LLM API from your own code (Anthropic, OpenAI, or open-source models) — a working prototype you can walk us through counts for more than a certificate.
• Message queues, caching (Redis), or any experience with systems that must stay up under load.
• Open-source contributions, side projects, hackathons, or competitive programming — anything that shows you write code when nobody is grading you.

HOW WE ASSESS

We will not ask you to invert a binary tree on a whiteboard. We will ask you to think in front of us.
• Code you can defend. Bring something you built. We will ask why you made each decision, not what the code does.
• Debugging under observation. We give you a broken thing. Your reasoning process matters more than your speed.
• Judgement under acceleration. You will use an AI assistant in the exercise. We are watching for whether you can tell when its output is right, when it is subtly wrong, and when it should be thrown away.
• Learning velocity. What did you learn in the last six months, how did you learn it, and what did you build with it
• Communication. Explain one technical decision to someone who is not an engineer. Clients will ask you to do this for real.

QUALIFICATIONS
• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related engineering or quantitative discipline.
• 1–3 years of professional software engineering experience. Strong internships, academic projects, or a substantial personal portfolio are considered for candidates at the lower end of that range.
• Professional working proficiency in English.

What We Value

We seek people who are:
• Ambitious, curious, and creative.
• Sincere and joyful in how they work.
• Passionate about delivering impact and creating value.
• Committed to integrity, excellence, and continuous improvement.
• Disciplined in execution, but flexible in learning.

Job Title: Senior Manager – Digital Product & Portfolio Management

Job Location: Jeddah, Saudi Arabia

1. Role Purpose

The Senior Manager – Digital Product & Portfolio Management manages and orchestrates a portfolio of digital products, platforms and business capabilities that enable digital sales growth, customer experience excellence, operational efficiency and transformation. The role provides central business-side product management and portfolio coordination, ensuring initiatives are clearly defined, strategically aligned, commercially justified, prioritized and delivered across an interconnected ecosystem.

Working with business stakeholders, Digital Technology, Architecture, UX/CX, Engineering, Data, Cybersecurity and external partners, the role translates opportunities and customer needs into structured capabilities, product requirements, roadmaps and executable delivery plans. It spans discovery, solution evaluation, backlog readiness, implementation coordination, launch readiness and post-launch optimization.

A key mandate is business-side orchestration of connected capabilities across eCommerce, CRM, customer engagement, Voice of Customer, analytics, AI, automation and partner platforms. The Senior Manager independently leads portfolio analysis, discovery, governance and cross-functional coordination, developing evidence-based recommendations for Director-led strategy, investment prioritization and major decisions. This is a hands-on product and portfolio role—not a traditional PMO or technical engineering role.

2. Key Responsibilities

A. Portfolio Strategy, Prioritization & Roadmaps
• Maintain an integrated portfolio roadmap across products, journeys, platforms and strategic initiatives.
• Assess initiatives against business value, customer impact, urgency, effort, readiness, risk, dependencies, reuse and strategic alignment.
• Recommend MVP scope, sequencing, release increments, trade-offs and investment priorities; prepare leadership decision materials.

B. Product Discovery & Business Capability Definition
• Lead discovery with business, customers, UX/CX, analytics, technology and delivery partners.
• Define problems, outcomes, customer journeys, use cases, capabilities, business rules, success measures and requirements.
• Produce business process flows and functional specifications; validate readiness before development.

C. Digital Capability & Ecosystem Orchestration
• Coordinate connected capabilities across eCommerce, CRM, engagement, VoC, analytics, AI, automation and partner ecosystems.
• Clarify platform responsibilities, system handoffs, integration dependencies, business ownership and reuse opportunities.
• Partner with Architecture and Engineering on platform-neutral solution options and cohesive end-to-end customer experiences.

D. Backlog, Requirements & Delivery Readiness
• Maintain product backlogs, epics, stories, acceptance criteria, release scope and requirement traceability.
• Lead refinement and resolve business ambiguities with Business Analysts, Product Owners and delivery teams.
• Assess scope changes and maintain documentation, decisions and ownership across product tools.

E. Cross-Functional Delivery & Product Lifecycle
• Coordinate business-side work from design and build through testing, launch, stabilization and optimization.
• Track dependencies, blockers, risks, scope and decisions across internal teams and vendors; escalate material issues.
• Support integrated release planning, demonstrations, business validation and transition into ongoing operations.

F. Technology & Solution Evaluation
• Work with Architecture and Engineering to evaluate build, buy, reuse and hybrid options against value, fit, integration, scalability, speed and cost.
• Support RFP requirements, evaluation criteria, vendor demonstrations and proof-of-concept assessments.
• Develop business-side recommendations without assuming technical architecture decision authority.

G. Customer Experience, Measurement & Optimization
• Champion usability, accessibility, localization, content readiness and consistent journeys.
• Define product success measures with functional owners and ensure analytics and feedback requirements are embedded.
• Review adoption, conversion, experience and operational performance; recommend post-launch improvements.

H. Portfolio Governance & Stakeholder Coordination
• Operate intake, assessment, prioritization, stage-gate, reporting and escalation processes under Director direction.
• Maintain portfolio visibility of ownership, scope, funding, risks, dependencies, decisions and approvals.
• Prepare executive updates, decision logs, governance forums and cross-functional alignment activities.

I. Financial, Resource & Vendor Support
• Support budgets, forecasts, business cases, capacity plans, procurement inputs and investment analysis.
• Coordinate vendor assessments and business-side performance reviews; monitor commitments and deliverables.
• Track planned versus realized benefits and recommend ways to improve platform and investment value.

J. Risk, Compliance & Release Readiness
• Coordinate inputs from cybersecurity, privacy, data protection, legal, accessibility, brand and quality control owners.
• Coordinate UAT, business and operational readiness, support arrangements, analytics readiness and acceptance evidence.
• Provide business go-live readiness recommendations and track defects and stabilization actions.

3. Qualifications & Experience

Mandatory
• Bachelor's degree in Business, Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Digital Business, Product Management or related field.
• 8–12+ years of relevant experience, including 3–5 years in senior digital product, platform or product portfolio responsibilities.
• Demonstrated hands-on ownership of discovery, roadmaps, prioritization, backlogs, requirements, cross-functional delivery and launch readiness.
• Experience managing multiple digital products or connected business capabilities in complex customer-facing environments.
• Understanding of SaaS ecosystems, API integrations and enterprise technology dependencies.
• Strong commercial analysis, stakeholder engagement, problem solving and executive communication.

Highly Preferred
• Digital commerce, B2B platforms, insurance, banking, fintech, telecommunications or similar transactional ecosystems.
• Experience across CRM, engagement, analytics, automation and integrated customer platforms; Salesforce, Sprinklr or Qualtrics exposure advantageous.
• Agile delivery tools such as Jira, Azure DevOps or Confluence; vendor and systems-integrator coordination.
• Digital analytics, conversion optimization, customer experience measurement and investment governance.

Preferred Certifications
• PSPO, CSPO, SAFe Product Manager/Product Owner or comparable product certification.
• Relevant Agile, portfolio or programme management certifications; practical product ownership matters more than certification alone.

4. Expected Deliverables
• Integrated digital product portfolio roadmap and prioritization framework.
• Product discovery outputs, business capability maps and cross-platform dependencies.
• Backlogs, requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria and release readiness assessments.
• Portfolio governance reporting, executive decision papers and investment recommendations.
• Vendor/solution evaluations, product performance and value-realization reports.

5. Key Performance Indicators
• Portfolio roadmap alignment and readiness; quality of discovery and requirements.
• Backlog readiness and reduction of requirement-related rework.
• Cross-platform dependency resolution and business launch readiness.
• Governance decision turnaround and stakeholder alignment.
• Product adoption and realized value against approved objectives.
• Targets and measurement methods will be set against the approved portfolio and operating model.

Responsibilities include user research, creating wireframes, prototypes, and mockups, conducting usability tests, and staying current with industry trends. A strong portfolio and proficiency with Sketch, Adobe XD or Figma are essential; knowledge of HTML/CSS is a plus.

About Noon
Noon is a Saudi EdTech company. Noon Track runs inside schools: a hybrid programme that prepares students for Qudrat (قدرات) and Tahsili (تحصيلي), the national university-admission exams. Our students are 15 to 17 years old. Noon is becoming an AI-native company, department by department, and the number of schools we serve is growing. We believe every student deserves world-class teachers. And to make it happen, we’re reimagining everything about education: from cutting-edge tech to peer learning and physical spaces that spark curiosity.
• Hear about our vision directly from our CEO here.

• Learn more about us [here]

The role
You will be the one designer who owns the student experience. Primarily that means the student app: where students study, work with an AI tutor, answer questions, and take part in activities, including games and head-to-head duels on a topic. You will also shape parts of the live classroom experience.
This is a Senior/Principal-level individual contributor Product Designer role. There is no design team underneath you and no manager drawing your roadmap. You take a problem from the first student conversation to the shipped screen, and you decide what to look at next.
Why this role
• One owner of the whole student experience, with a direct line to leadership.

• Speed: with AI in the workflow, ideas go from research to release in days, not quarters.

• An experimentation practice being built from the ground up, with you shaping it.

• A company expanding into more schools, with a long-term ambition to match.

What you will do
• Spend real time with students in Saudi schools. Interviews, focus groups, classroom observation. Turn what you hear into design decisions, and go back to check them.

• Design for Saudi Arabia, not for the generic "best practice" app. Patterns that work in London or San Francisco often fail here. You know why, and you can show it in your work.

• Own the student app end to end. Flows, information architecture, prototypes, final UI, and the handover to engineering.

• Design activities students want to come back to, games and duels included, with learning as the gate: an activity that is more fun but teaches less is a regression.

• Run experiments. State a hypothesis, build the variants, agree the metric, and read the result honestly. You will help build the experimentation practice, not just use it.

• Work AI-native. Use AI tools for generation, prototyping and production so your time goes to research and judgement. We care about the quality of your decisions, not how many pixels you pushed by hand.

• Work directly with the product manager and engineers. Short loops, fast releases, no layers.

About you (To be successful in this role, you should have):
• Roughly 5 years of experience in UX, product design experience. We care less about the number and more about how many people you have interviewed and what you did with it.

• A research practice you can describe in detail: how you recruit, what you ask, how you synthesise, how it reached the product.

• A portfolio of projects that demonstrate your creativity and delivery of results through great consumer-facing mobile-first experiences

• Proficiency in using various tools and techniques to create and communicate your design ideas, such as sketches, wireframes, mockups, prototypes, etc.

• Experience in conducting user research and testing in different contexts and cultures, using both qualitative and quantitative methods

• A strong sense of empathy, curiosity, and creativity, and a willingness to learn and experiment

Nice to have:
• Game design or gaming industry experience.

• Large-scale B2C or e-commerce experience, where A/B tests and small-metric optimisation were the daily rhythm.

• Enough front-end to prototype in code with AI assistance.

Why Noon?
• Real impact — your work directly affects how thousands of students learn every day.

• Speed and autonomy — small team, big problems, zero bureaucracy.

• AI-native culture — we don't just talk about AI, we build with it daily.

• Well-funded — Series B closed, substantial recurring revenue, and accelerating.

• Mission that matters — every student deserves world-class teachers. We're making it happen.

Benefits
In addition to a competitive base salary, we offer:
• Performance-based bonus

• 21 days of annual leave

• Full premium Medical coverage, including Family Dependent

Soum is a fast-growing B2C marketplace based in Riyadh, connecting buyers and sellers of used electronics and used cars across Saudi Arabia through our website and mobile app. Everything we do is built on trust: buyers need confidence in what they are getting, and sellers need confidence they will be paid fairly and quickly. About the Role
The Consumer Product Manager owns the experience our customers touch every day: how buyers discover, evaluate, pay for and receive a used phone or car, and how sellers list, price and get paid for what they sell. You will be the voice of the Soum customer inside the product team, turning deep consumer insight into features that grow conversion, repeat purchase and trust in the platform.

You will work across the app and web, partnering with design, engineering, operations and commercial teams to ship quickly and learn from what we ship.

•
Own the roadmap for a core consumer area (such as the buyer journey, the seller journey or subscriptions), prioritising ruthlessly by impact on conversion, retention, GMV and customer trust.

•
Build a deep, continuous understanding of Soum's customers through user interviews, usability testing, app reviews, customer support tickets and behavioural data.

•
Optimise the end-to-end marketplace funnel: listing creation, search and discovery, product pages, checkout and payments (Mada, Apple Pay, BNPL), delivery tracking, returns and post-purchase experience.

Design and improve trust features that make buying used feel safe, including device condition grading, car inspection reports, verified sellers, buyer protection, ratings and transparent pricing.

Shape the subscription products for electronics and cars: the value proposition, packaging, onboarding, engagement and retention, working closely with Commercial and Finance on unit economics.

Translate problems into clear PRDs, user stories and acceptance criteria, and run agile delivery with design and engineering, from discovery through release and iteration.

Champion an Arabic-first, bilingual experience with high-quality RTL design and localisation for Saudi customers.

Run a disciplined experimentation practice: form hypotheses, design A/B tests, define success metrics and make fast, evidence-based decisions on what to scale or kill.

•
Monitor and report on core consumer KPIs, including conversion rate, listing-to-sale rate, activation, repeat purchase, subscription retention, NPS and customer complaints.

•
Partner cross-functionally with Operations (inspection, logistics, customer service), Marketing and Growth (acquisition, CRM), and Finance to make sure product changes work end to end, not just on screen.

Keep a close eye on regional and global marketplaces and recommerce players, and bring the best ideas back to Soum, adapted for our customers.

Requirements

•
2–4 years of product management experience on consumer-facing digital products such as marketplaces, e-commerce, fintech or consumer apps.

•
A proven track record of shipping consumer features that moved measurable business metrics, and the ability to explain exactly how.

•
Strong consumer intuition backed by data: comfortable with product analytics tools (e.g. Amplitude, Mixpanel, GA4), funnel analysis and A/B testing; working SQL is a strong plus.

Hands-on experience building for mobile (iOS and Android) and web.

Solid understanding of two-sided marketplace dynamics, including supply and demand balance, liquidity, trust and pricing.

Experience working closely with designers and engineers in an agile environment, with clear written specs and sharp prioritisation.

Nice to Have

Experience with KSA or GCC consumers, Arabic/RTL products and local payment methods.

•
Background in used goods, recommerce, automotive or subscription businesses.
